title: Strata-priority batching exploration and quickplay notes
content:
Purpose / quick summary:

This is an experimental scratchpad for a different angle on continuous batching tuning: stratified priority windows. Goal: reduce p99 tail for mixed-SLO workloads without excessive p50 regression or utilization loss. We try to capture effects that previous runs (see other notes) missed: interaction between rare long-sequence requests, KV-cache warmup, and small high-priority traffic spikes.

Hypothesis:
- Splitting the request queue into 2–4 strata by estimated token length and priority will reduce head-of-line blocking when large requests arrive.
- Use adaptive timeouts per-stratum (timeout = base * sqrt(stratum_size_factor)) to reduce unnecessary waits for small requests while letting large batches form when needed.
- Apply a lightweight fairness token (Jain-style) to avoid starving low-priority background jobs.

Experiment matrix (what we ran):
- Workloads: A (chatty, 8–32 tokens typical), B (assistant, 64–512 tokens mixed), C (long completion, 1024–4096 tokens) injected at different ratios.
- Strata configs: 2-strata (small/large), 3-strata (tiny/small/large), 4-strata (tiny/small/med/large).
- Priority levels: high (interactive), normal (background productivity), low (batch embedding).
- Timeout multipliers: 0.5x, 1x (base 4ms), 2x, 4x.
- Batch size caps per-stratum: 8, 16, 32, 64.
- KV-cache warmup policies: aggressive (prefetch top-k keys for warmed sessions) vs lazy.

Metrics collected (per run):
- p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (server-side, request-to-first-token and request-to-last-token)
- tokens/sec and GPU utilization (nvidia-smi sample + runtime telemetry)
- batch occupancy (avg batch size, fraction of empty/vs-full batches)
- fairness index computed per-minute across priorities (Jain index of throughput)
- cost proxy: GPU-ms per 1k tokens
- cold-start event count (KV-cache miss, new session)

Key instrumentation additions for these runs (short):
- added per-request field estimate_tokens at admission time (from prompt-metadata or quick tokenizer estimate)
- added stratum_id tag to tracing spans and metrics exported to metrics pipeline
- simple fairness counter that weights high-prio requests 2x in admission if starvation detected

Representative run summary (mixed-ratio: 70% A, 20% B, 10% C) - 3-strata, adaptive timeouts (base 4ms, mult per stratum 0.5/1/2), batch caps 16/32/64, KV-prefetch: aggressive:
- p50: 12ms (down 1ms vs baseline continuous-batch)
- p95: 48ms (down 6ms)
- p99: 210ms (down 65ms)
- GPU utilization: 68% (baseline 74%)
- avg batch occupancy (all strata combined): 28 tokens / batch (vs baseline 34)
- fairness index: 0.92 (baseline 0.78) -> meaning less starvation for low-priority background
- cost proxy: +3% GPU-ms per 1k tokens (higher due to extra micro-batches / lower packing)
- notable: KV-cache miss rate for long sessions dropped 18% (prefetch worked)

Interpretation notes:
- Tail reduction came primarily from the small-strata timeout reduction: small interactive requests rarely waited for large tokens and thus avoided being stuck behind long-seqs being formed.
- The medium/large strata still allow good packing for long-running requests so throughput remained acceptable.
- Slight utilization drop is expected; tradeoff: lower tail -> better SLO compliance for interactive customers.
- Fairness index improvement suggests priority-weighting prevented starvation for background jobs. Must validate across different ratios (we saw fairness drop when C went to 25% of traffic).

Surprising behaviors / outliers observed:
- When aggressive KV-prefetch + large-strata batch cap 64 used, sometimes cold-start long requests created transient queue lock for ~300ms because prefetch triggered a GPU micro-scheduling delay; mitigated by spreading prefetch tasks on a separate CPU threadpool with backoff.
- Microburst of 200 high-priority tiny requests caused more small-batch churn than expected; adding a quick 1–2ms debounce before admission for tiny-strata smoothed the effect.
- A pathological mix (10% C but 80% of C were 4096-token worst-case) still produced p99 > 500ms; suggests we need secondary policy: fall back to an alternate model variant (quantized long-infer) for ultra-long requests.

Profiling pointers / logs to inspect:
- sample trace ids: trace-20260204-0532-A1, trace-20260209-1147-B4 (search in tracing/serving-runtime).
- perf hotspots: kernel selection / cuBLAS matmul accounted for 62% of GPU time on long sequences; scheduling overhead accounted for ~9% on small requests.
- CPU-side: admission lock contention peaked at 1.8k QPS in one run (stack: admit_worker -> stratum_enqueue -> wait_for_batch). Consider sharded enqueue per-stratum to reduce contention.

Commands / scripts used (for reproducibility):
- loadgen: tools/loadgen_mixed.py --profile A:0.7,B:0.2,C:0.1 --rate 600 --seed 42 --kv-prefetch aggressive --strata-config 3,4,64 --timeout-mults 0.5,1,2
- local run: PYENV=3.10 ./ci/run_strata_experiment.sh --config experiments/strata/three_strata_adaptive.yaml --collect-metrics
- query tracing: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TRACING_KEY" https://tracing.redwood.internal/api/trace/trace-20260204-0532-A1

Recommendations / next steps:
1) Sanity run across different ratios: specifically 50/30/20 and 80/15/5 to validate fairness holds.
2) Add a cheap model-variant fallback policy: if estimated tokens > 2000, route to q4-long variant with looser quality threshold. Track quality/regression via eval set.
3) Implement stratum-sharded enqueue workers to cut admission contention spikes.
4) Re-run with KV-prefetch conservative mode (cap concurrent prefetches to N) to see if GPU micro-scheduling artifact disappears.
5) Prepare a customer-impact proposal: enable 3-strata adaptive default for hosted interactive tier with rollout (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%) and metric guardrails (p50 p99 + cost delta).

Open questions / trade-offs to resolve:
- How large a utilization hit is tolerable per customer tier? We need product guidance: SRE/Prod should set target max +5% GPU-ms per 1k tokens for latency-first tiers.
- How to version stratum logic so Private deployments can opt out (policy flag in config)?
- Should we expose stratum hints via API (developer-provided estimated_tokens) or rely on runtime tokenizer estimation? Security/abuse surface?

Action items (owners):
- Marcus: implement enqueue sharding POC (due 2026-03-10)
- Evelyn: add conservative KV-prefetch cap and rerun the 3-strata matrix (due 2026-03-05)
- Jonah: prep a short canary rollout playbook and metric dashboard (due 2026-03-12)
- Aisha (me): consolidate results and draft a short internal memo for product on suggested default (due 2026-03-15)

Appendix: quick notes on fairness measurement implementation:
- We compute per-minute throughput for each priority p_i, then Jain index = (sum p_i)^2 / (n * sum p_i^2). Reported 0..1, closer to 1 -> more equal. Weight high-prio by 2x in the numerator if we want intentional bias but still compute raw index as well.

Raw sample data snippets (CSV lines):

Notes for the write-up: keep this doc as a living experiment log. When we finalize we can extract a cleaned runbook and a short product-facing one-pager.

---
Scratch ideas (low friction experiments to try):
- Hybrid admission: tiny requests (<16 tokens) get a tiny immediate-cold-path that prioritizes <8ms latency even if it produces 20% more micro-batches. Switch on per-tenant toggle.
- Predictive batching: use a very cheap ML model that predicts completion length from prompt features in 0.2ms and drives stratum assignment. Compare cost vs tokenizer heuristics.
- Fairness SLA: expose a tenant-level fairness SLA that guarantees a minimum throughput fraction for background workloads (requires metering and billing alignment).

End of doc.
